newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady, trade livelier.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady, trade livelier.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates held their ground on Tuesday as trade livened up on Zagreb's money market amid growing demand for kuna funds, dealers said.
"Banks hope that a central bank's auction (of hard currency) on Wednesday will get them enough kuna funds for Friday, that is for regular end-of-week payments," one dealer said.
Banks also slightly increased their Lombard borrowing from the central bank to 126.7 million kuna from 106.7 on Monday.
Their overall balances of the banking sector rose to 666 million kuna on Monday, up from last week's 450 million. This boosted interbank money market supply to more than 110 million.
No banks reported any shortfalls at the end of the day.
This morning's trade reached 43.3 million kuna, most of which were call money loans at an unchanged 7.0 percent.
"So far banks are mostly seeking short-term loans," the dealer said, putting a surplus in trade at 70 million kuna.
One smaller two-week loan was granted at 9.0 percent and a 30-day loan at 13 percent.
The 31-day prices were 9.0 and 11 percent, with a foreign bank accepting a lower price.
